# 陸氏易解

**Source:** 四庫全書 文淵閣版, V7.4, p185
**Extent:** 1 卷
**Base edition:** WYG

## Authors / Editors
- 陸績 (吳朝) 撰
- 姚士粦 (明朝) 輯

**Editions:** WYG

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A Míng-period reconstruction of the lost *Yì* commentary of [陸績](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B8%E7%B8%BE) Lù Jì of Wú, in one *juàn*, by [姚士粦](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A7%9A%E5%A3%AB%E7%B2%A6) Yáo Shìlín of Hǎiyán 海鹽 (modern northern Zhèjiāng). The original of Lù Jì's *Yì* commentary is recorded variously in the early bibliographies — *Sānguó zhì · Wúzhì* lists it as *Yì shì xuán* 易釋玄, the *Suíshū jīngjí zhì* as *Zhōuyì zhù* 周易注 in fifteen *juàn*, and [陸德明](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B8%E5%BE%B7%E6%98%8E) Lù Démíng's *Jīngdiǎn shìwén xùlù* 經典釋文序錄 (with the *Xīn / Jiù Tángshū* concurring) as *Zhōuyì shù* 周易述 in thirteen *juàn* plus a *Huìtōng* 會通 in one *juàn* — and was wholly lost in transmission. Yáo Shìlín gathered 150 fragments, and the work was first printed in the late-Míng *Yányì zhì lín* 鹽邑志林 collection (Hǎiyán's local scholarly anthology). The Sìkù *tiyao* corrects [朱彝尊](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%B1%E5%BD%9D%E5%B0%8A) Zhū Yízūn's *Jīngyì kǎo* 經義考, which had alleged that Yáo merely scissored together passages from Lù Démíng's *Shìwén* and [李鼎祚](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E9%BC%8E%E7%A5%9A) Lǐ Dǐngzuò's *Jíjiě*: in fact a substantial proportion of Yáo's fragments come from the *Jīng shì Yì zhuàn zhù* 京氏易傳注 of [京房](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BA%AC%E6%88%BF) Jīng Fáng, a source Zhū had overlooked.

This is the third of the *Sìkù* trio of opening-section *jíyì* recompilations, in deliberate parallel to [KR1a0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0003) and [KR1a0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0004). The catalog dynasty is 吳 by the Sìkù convention that recompilations of lost works are filed under the original author's dynasty; the actual composition window of the surviving recension is the late Wànlì 萬曆 era of the late Míng (ca. 1590–1620), notBefore being a rough lower bound for Yáo Shìlín's mature scholarly activity in Hǎiyán under Yáo's literary-circle patron [胡震亨](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%83%A1%E9%9C%87%E4%BA%A8) Hú Zhènhēng, notAfter the conventional terminus for the *Yányì zhì lín* compilation.

**Abstract**

[陸績](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B8%E7%B8%BE) Lù Jì (ca. 188–219), of Wú prefecture (modern Sūzhōu), was a child prodigy of the Wú-Hàn period (the *xiào jǐn* 孝謹 anecdote of his hiding three oranges in his sleeve at age six to take home to his mother is widely circulated in pre-modern moralising literature). He served the Sūn 孫 court as Grand Administrator of Yùlín 鬱林 commandery (in modern Guǎngxī) with concurrent appointment as Lieutenant General; the *Sānguó zhì · Wúzhì* (juan 57) gives him a brief but laudatory biography. He was a leading representative of the Hàn-style *Yì* current at Wú: his commentary belonged squarely to the *xiàngshù* 象數 line and was extensively cited by [李鼎祚](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E9%BC%8E%E7%A5%9A) Lǐ Dǐngzuò ([KR1a0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0008)) and [陸德明](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B8%E5%BE%B7%E6%98%8E) Lù Démíng. The early bibliographic record shows the original at variable length — fifteen *juàn* in the *Suíshū*, thirteen plus a *Huìtōng* of one *juàn* in the *Jīngdiǎn shìwén* and the Tang histories — but the work was lost between the Táng and the Sòng.

[姚士粦](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A7%9A%E5%A3%AB%E7%B2%A6) Yáo Shìlín (*zì* Shūxiáng 叔祥, fl. late Wànlì), of Hǎiyán 海鹽, was a member of the literary circle of [胡震亨](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%83%A1%E9%9C%87%E4%BA%A8) Hú Zhènhēng and contributed several reconstructions of pre-Hàn and Hàn texts to the *Yányì zhì lín* anthology compiled there. The biographical anecdote — orphaned at thirteen, illiterate at twenty, taught reading by his Jiāng-family hosts in Déqīng, eventually a self-taught scholar of consequence — is reported in [周亮工](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%91%A8%E4%BA%AE%E5%B7%A5) Zhōu Liànggōng's *Shū yǐng* and was sufficiently striking that the Sìkù editors retell it in the *tiyao*. His other notable *jíyì* contributions in *Yányì zhì lín* include the *Hàn shì shàngshū* 韓氏尚書 ([韓嬰](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%9F%93%E5%AC%B0) Hán Yīng *Shū*) reconstructions and a number of pre-Hàn philosophical fragments.

The Sìkù *tiyao* explicitly weighs Yáo's compilation against Wáng Yīnglín's, judges it less thorough than Wáng's Zhèng [KR1a0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0003) but still useful as a witness to Lù Jì's *Yì*, and notes (against Zhū Yízūn) that Yáo's principal under-credited source is the *Jīng shì Yìzhuàn zhù* — making this also a useful indirect witness to Jīng Fáng's *Yì*.
